narrative: Material PL3__M1427F84 exhibits lumpy demand (CV=0.62, non-zero fraction=79%) with no detectable trend over the 228-day observation window (March 2025 – March 2026). Lead times are variable (CV=0.39, ranging 1.63–6.08 days), making lead-time uncertainty the dominant variance driver (56.4% of sigma_LTD). The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock, leaving the operation fully exposed; the recommended (r,Q) policy introduces a 5,997-unit buffer at 95% service level with a storage-capacity-capped order quantity of 35,354 units, reducing annual costs by 61.4%.
warnings: EOQ of 53,200 units exceeds storage capacity after accounting for safety stock; order quantity capped to 35,354 units (floor(41351.782 - 5997)). Capacity utilization is at 99.998%, leaving only 0.78 units of headroom — any safety stock increase requires storage capacity review.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Lumpy demand with variable lead times is best served by a continuous-review (r,Q) policy that triggers replenishment based on actual inventory position breaching the reorder point, rather than a periodic review that could miss stockout windows between review cycles.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds the EOQ (53,200 → 35,354 units), increasing annual orders from ~10 to ~15 and raising ordering cost from ~$773 to ~$1,160. Service level is maintained at 95% but capacity headroom is only 0.78 units — operationally, this is a hard constraint that must be monitored.
